column3: Directly states enduring punishment with neither relief nor reprieve.
Shows Fire's inhabitants seeking exit yet remaining in its lasting punishment.
Directly frames recompense as the return due to the ungrateful.
Repeats the unrelieved, unpostponed punishment already established by 2:162.
The immediate continuation adds cries for release, refused opportunity, and tasting.
Those in Fire reduce their request to a single day of relief.
Depicts Jahannam as an enclosing punishment returned to wrongdoers.
Adds the local surah's delayed accounting for what people have earned.
Offers a secondary instance of recompense linked to rejection or ingratitude.
Reiterates that punishment will not be lightened, with little beyond prior exact parallels.
Its doubled experience across life and death only remotely illuminates the withheld death.
A completed mortal death provides a distant contrast to the focus's nonterminal punishment.
Links disbelief with abiding in the Fire of Jahannam.
Knowledge of hidden interiors does not by itself add to Fire or recompense.
Connects disbelievers to severe punishment and complements the focus's stated cause.
A prayer to be turned from Jahannam supplies a limited contrast to its imposed punishment.
The warning against worldly deception does not specify the focus's punishment mechanism.
The wish for death to have ended everything clarifies why nonterminal punishment matters.
Connects disbelief and eventual gathering to Jahannam without specifying its distinctive conditions.
Presents persons being tested directly upon the Fire.
The denial of coming punishment supplies only a contrary stance.
Dying in disbelief supplies background for a punitive outcome but not its form.
The local continuation makes disbelief itself accumulate loss and divine displeasure.
Links dying as a disbeliever to prepared painful punishment after repentance is unavailable.
Adds concrete Fire imagery assigned specifically to disbelievers.
The local historical warning supports consequence for prior peoples only generally.
A favorable postmortem provision is a distant contrast to the focus's punishment.
Directly joins punishment without relief to failed help or rescue.
States the accounting principle: each self is repaid solely for its deeds.
Its warning against disbelief after granted security lacks the focus's punitive result.
The closed Fire reinforces the focus's absence of an exit.
The local principle that evil plotting returns to its authors only generally supports recompense.
Turning away leads to an arduous punishment, without the focus's enduring Fire conditions.
Positive recompense for beneficence does not materially clarify this punitive recompense.
The messenger's warning role supplies background for culpable rejection.
Divine legal easing is a contrast to the punishment that receives no easing.
This repeats positive recompense without adding to the focus.
Makes acquired action the exact basis of individual recompense without injustice.
Disbelief followed by eventual knowledge supplies a limited warning context.
Associates disbelief with ruin and the nullification of works, but not Fire's conditions.
The local summons to remember divine gifts sharpens the focus's charge of ingratitude.
States a full recompense principle that supports the focus's formula of return.
Another positive-recompense formula adds no punitive detail.
The command to taste punishment gives direct experiential form to the focus's torment.
Fear of punishment is only an antecedent response, not its nature or cause.
A destroyed criminal people illustrates recompense generally, outside the focus's lasting Fire.
Mercy withheld offers only an indirect contrast to relief withheld in punishment.
Names turning away and disbelief but does not add their consequence.
God's true judgment supports final settlement only at a general level.
Fire, equal outcome regardless of endurance, and recompense for deeds make punishment inescapable.
Warns disbelievers of their promised day without defining the punishment.
Pairs return for judgment with painful punishment for disbelief.
Revelation's truth and divine awareness supply only background to culpable rejection.
Rescue from painful punishment is a limited opposite to the focus's settled punishment.
Contrasts believers with treacherous ingratitude but gives no corresponding outcome.
Turns the anticipated ordeal into an order to taste the punishment they demanded.
Identifies disbelievers by rejection of signs but adds no Fire or repayment detail.
Divine judgment between disputants is only a general accounting parallel.
The local seizure of disbelievers gives a concrete consequence within the surah's gratitude thread.
Its light and heavy language concerns mobilization, not punishment being lightened.
Shows ingratitude after experienced rescue, clarifying the focus's moral charge indirectly.
True weighing offers a remote accounting parallel without the punitive outcome.
Directly commands tasting everlasting punishment as recompense for what was done.
The garden consumed by fire is a parable, not a link to the focus's punishment.
Grateful praise after sorrow is removed is a limited reversal of unrelieved torment.
A general reminder of punishment and warning adds little after direct tasting parallels.
Names a scorching Fire but supplies no cause, duration, or absence of relief.
Promises severe tasted punishment and return for the worst of disbelievers' deeds.
Its rebuke at human ingratitude illuminates cause but not the stated recompense.
The completion of revelation is unrelated to the focus's judgment or punishment.
Human dependence on God gives background for why gratitude matters in the local surah.
Identifies disbelievers as persisting in denial without adding consequence.
Provision, dispute, and eventual judgment give only a distant gratitude-and-accounting link.
Directly calls Fire the eternal dwelling and recompense for denying divine signs.
Divine control of life and death only distantly frames the focus's withheld death.
Links received mercy and human ingratitude but supplies no punitive settlement.
Defers recompense for acquired deeds to God, preserving individual settlement.
States severe punishment after futile opposition without the focus's key conditions.
Judgment after knowledgeable disagreement is a general parallel only.
Adds equal repayment, no protector, and eternal residence in Fire for earned evil.
A general recompense formula in a positive setting adds little to punitive return.
Describes human ingratitude after mercy is withdrawn, without its final consequence.
Directly unites tasting everlasting punishment with repayment for acquired deeds.
Prepared painful punishment for wrongdoers lacks the focus's nonrelief and nondeath details.
Removing burdens from believers is an indirect contrast to torment that is not lightened.
The ironic command to taste punishment adds a narrow experiential echo.
Continued denial identifies the focus's cause but adds no consequence.
The revival image does not materially illuminate punishment or its recompense.
Uses disbelief in a particular accusation without a punitive or accounting connection.
Universal mortality gives only a distant contrast to death withheld in the Fire.
Just judgment among communities is a general accounting parallel.
Blessing across birth, death, and resurrection does not clarify the focus.
Associates disbelief with harmful gain and no afterlife share, but not the focus's punishment.
Positive recompense after obedience does not add to the focus.
The legal waiting period after death has no relevant punitive connection.
God's power over life and death does not specify the focus's exceptional nondeath.
Final judgment and the lack of a way for disbelievers provide a remote settlement parallel.
Makes denial of signs and resurrection the cause of a stated recompense, complementing the focus's disbelief.
Denial and following desire lack a stated punishment or accounting result here.
A prophetic warning of a great-day punishment supplies only broad antecedent context.
Directly makes disbelief and denial of signs the basis for abiding in Fire.
Shows those in punishment unable to leave the Fire.
Places disbelievers among the companions of Fire, abiding there.
The repeated renewal of burned skins makes punishment's continuing experience concrete.
Names Jahannam as the refuge from which no way out is found.
Shows that no ransom can avert the painful punishment of disbelievers.
Connects disbelief to a painful punishment that must be endured.
Describes Fire as the lasting abode for its inhabitants.
Directly pairs denial of signs with eternal residence in Fire.
Adds the entry of successive rejecting communities into Fire and its doubled punishment.
States that denial of signs is repaid only according to what was done.
Commands rejection's party to taste the punishment of burning.
Directly assigns the Fire of Jahannam as an eternal punishment.
Promises hypocrites and disbelievers the enduring Fire of Jahannam.
Makes Fire the abiding destination earned through prior action.
Links disbelief to a severe punishment after a brief worldly enjoyment.
Depicts the wretched as dwelling in Fire with its sustained bodily condition.
Places Jahannam before the rejecter and adds a tormenting drink.
States that death comes from every direction but is not accomplished.
Declares Jahannam the promised gathering place for the errant.
Commands the arrogant to enter the gates of Jahannam to abide there.
Every time the Fire subsides, its blaze is increased, sharply negating relief.
Images Fire as an enclosing barrier and its drink as a painful consequence.
Directly says the criminal in Hell neither dies nor lives.
Connects excess and disbelief in signs with a more enduring punishment.
Makes the disbelievers and their objects of worship fuel for Jahannam.
Adds bodily punishment within Fire through iron implements and scalding fluid.
Shows every attempted exit from anguish returning its inhabitants to Fire and tasting.
Those whose scales are light lose themselves and abide in Jahannam.
The Fire's rage and roar make its punitive presence vivid before entry.
Adds confinement in a narrow place and the cry for destruction.
States that Jahannam surrounds the disbelievers.
Every attempt to leave Fire is reversed with the command to taste its punishment.
Curses disbelievers and prepares for them a blazing Fire.
Commands entry into Jahannam as the consequence of disbelief.
Depicts disbelievers driven in groups to Jahannam and confronted with fulfilled warning.
Adds continual exposure to Fire followed by entry into the severest punishment.
States that the guilty remain in Jahannam's punishment.
Explicitly says the punishment is not lightened and they despair within it.
Names Fire as the refuge and denies any exit from it.
Identifies Jahannam as the Fire denied by the guilty.
Shows its inhabitants moving between Fire and scalding water.
Denies ransom and makes Fire the final refuge of the hypocrites and disbelievers.
Assigns the punishment of Jahannam to those who disbelieve in their Lord.
Connects disobedience and denial to abiding in the Fire.
Portrays Jahannam as an ambush awaiting transgressors.
Adds remaining in it for long ages.
States that punishment only increases for those who denied the accounting.
Places the wretched in the greatest Fire.
Directly says its inhabitant neither dies nor lives.
